# Noise and kit audio assertion helpers

**Parent:** TF-0MVEWKZ1R0011VFZ | **Type:** task

> **Goal:** As a maintainer, I want shared, proven analysis assertions for noise-based and percussive renders, so every later feature in this epic asserts audibility, spectral character and decay with the same honest measurements instead of ad-hoc per-test heuristics.

## Context

`src/instruments/__tests__/helpers.ts` already provides `renderNoteSequence`, `computePeak`, `computeRms`, `isSilent`, `estimateDominantFrequency` (zero-crossing) and is proven by `harness.test.ts`. Noise-based voices have no single dominant frequency, so distinctness must be measured by **band energy** and **decay**, not zero crossings. The platform already ships FFT and envelope extractors (`computeMagnitudeSpectrum`, `SpectralCentroidExtractor`, `AttackTimeExtractor`, `TimeDomainExtractor`) under `src/analyze/` — reuse them rather than re-implementing analysis.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `helpers.ts` gains reusable helpers: `computeBandEnergy(samples, lowHz, highHz, sampleRate?)` (summed FFT magnitude energy in a frequency band), `computeDecayTime(samples, options?)` (seconds from peak until the envelope falls below a ratio of peak and stays there), and `describeSpectralDifference(a, b, sampleRate?)` returning a structured comparison (centroid delta + low/mid/high band-energy ratios) with a documented "distinct" verdict.
2. Every new helper delegates to the existing `src/analyze` extractors / FFT utilities where one exists — no duplicated FFT, RMS or silence-threshold implementation.
3. `harness.test.ts` proves each helper against synthetic signals with known answers: a 440 Hz sine reports a centroid within 5% of 440 Hz; a low-pass-shaped buffer reports more low-band than high-band energy (and the reverse for a high-pass one); a 0.2 s decaying burst reports a decay time of 0.2 s ±10%; identical buffers are not reported distinct while clearly different buffers are.
4. Helpers are test infrastructure only — no production module imports them; build and the instruments test scope stay green.
5. All new docblocks, comments and error messages are UK English.

## Minimal implementation

- Extend `helpers.ts` with the band-energy, decay-time and spectral-difference helpers (built on `computeMagnitudeSpectrum` + `TimeDomainExtractor`).
- Extend `harness.test.ts` with the synthetic-signal proofs above.
- Document the helpers in the file header so later features discover them.

## Constraints

- No production behaviour change and no new runtime dependency; browser-safe imports only.
- Keep the existing helper API and docblocks intact — other tests depend on them.

**Key Files:**

- `src/instruments/__tests__/helpers.ts` — **Extend.** Band-energy, decay-time and spectral-difference helpers.
- `src/instruments/__tests__/harness.test.ts` — **Extend.** Synthetic-signal proofs for each new helper.
- `src/analyze/extractors/spectral-centroid.ts` — **Reuse.** Spectral centroid over the FFT magnitude spectrum.
- `src/analyze/extractors/attack-time.ts` — **Reuse.** Transient/threshold measurement reference.
data.title: Noise and kit audio assertion helpers

# Shared seeded noise buffer module

**Parent:** TF-0MVEWKZ1R0011VFZ | **Type:** task

> **Goal:** As a sound designer, I want one shared, seeded white/pink/brown noise generator reusable from both ToneGraph recipes and instrument voices, so noise stays deterministic and is never duplicated.

## Context

`src/core/tonegraph.ts` has a private `generateNoiseBuffer(ctx, durationSeconds, color, rng)` implementing white, pink (Paul Kellet filter bank) and brown noise against the injected seeded `Rng` from `src/core/rng.ts` (`createRng(seed)`). It is not importable, so the instrument engine would otherwise duplicate it. ToneGraph recipe output is pinned by existing tests and must stay **byte-identical** when the function moves.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `src/audio/noise.ts` exports the generator as a reusable module: a `NoiseColor = "white" | "pink" | "brown"` type, `generateNoiseBuffer(ctx, durationSeconds, color, rng)`, and a colour guard that rejects unknown colours with an actionable UK-English error naming the accepted values.
2. `src/core/tonegraph.ts` imports the shared generator and holds **no local copy** of the noise algorithm; ToneGraph `noise` node output stays byte-identical — the existing `src/core/tonegraph.test.ts` noise/determinism tests pass unchanged.
3. Unit tests prove: same seed ⇒ byte-identical samples; different seeds ⇒ different samples; every colour is non-silent and stays within [-1, 1]; colours are spectrally ordered as documented (white centroid > pink centroid > brown centroid); unknown-colour rejection names the accepted values.
4. `src/audio/noise.ts` pulls in no Node-only (`node:*`) import transitively, so it is safe in a browser bundle.
5. All comments, docblocks and error messages are UK English.

## Minimal implementation

- Move the generator and colour type into `src/audio/noise.ts` verbatim (float-for-float), with docblocks describing each colour's filter.
- Replace the ToneGraph local function with an import; keep the call site, `durationHint` behaviour and RNG draw order identical.
- Add the determinism / spectrum / validation tests.

## Constraints

- **Byte-identical ToneGraph output is the hard gate** — do not retune the pink or brown filters in this item.
- `ctx.createBuffer` plus the seeded `rng` only; no new runtime dependencies.

**Key Files:**

- `src/audio/noise.ts` — **New.** Shared seeded noise-buffer generator + colour guard.
- `src/audio/noise.test.ts` — **New.** Determinism, spectrum and validation tests.
- `src/core/tonegraph.ts` — **Refactor.** Import the shared generator; delete the local copy.
- `src/core/tonegraph.test.ts` — **Verify.** Existing noise determinism tests stay green unchanged.
- `src/core/rng.ts` — **Reuse.** `createRng(seed)` seeded RNG.

# Noise oscillator vertical slice

**Parent:** TF-0MVEWKZ1R0011VFZ | **Type:** feature

> **Goal:** As a sound designer, I want to declare an instrument whose oscillator is white/pink/brown noise — `oscillator: { type: "noise", color, seed? }` — so snares, hats, claps and foley can be synthesised inside the existing instrument schema, deterministically, on both the offline and real-time paths.

## Context

`src/instruments/schema.ts` currently restricts `oscillator.type` to `sine | square | sawtooth | triangle` (`OSCILLATOR_WAVES`). `src/instruments/engine.ts` builds `OscillatorNode`s in `buildVoiceNodes`, schedules them in `scheduleOfflineVoice` (`start`/`stop`) and stores `{ gain, oscillator }` per live voice in `createRealtimeInstrument`. Noise needs an `AudioBufferSourceNode` with the same start/stop contract, fed by the shared seeded generator from the "Shared seeded noise buffer module" child. Operator decision (Appendix Q4): the seed lives on the oscillator, optional, with a fixed default.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `validateInstrumentDefinition` accepts `oscillator: { type: "noise", color: "white" | "pink" | "brown", seed?: number }` and returns a narrowed/typed oscillator; validation rejects an unknown colour and a non-integer or out-of-range seed with actionable UK-English errors naming the offending field and accepted values.
2. Offline rendering (`renderInstrument`) of a noise instrument produces **non-silent, deterministic** output: same definition + seed + note sequence ⇒ byte-identical samples; changing only the seed changes the samples; changing only the colour changes the samples.
3. The noise voice honours the ADSR envelope and optional filter exactly like an oscillator voice: a fast-decay envelope reaches (and stays at) the sustain level, a release returns to silence, and a low-pass filter measurably reduces high-band energy relative to the unfiltered render.
4. The real-time path (`createRealtimeInstrument`) builds a startable/stoppable noise source (internal node union widened from `OscillatorNode`), starts it at note-on, releases and stops it at note-off, and its live-voice bookkeeping behaves as before (voice stealing still releases the stolen voice).
5. Every existing oscillator-only behaviour is untouched: the committed golden hashes in `src/instruments/__tests__/fixtures/determinism-hashes.json` are unchanged and `determinism.test.ts` stays green without regeneration.
6. Tests cover the schema accept/reject matrix, offline determinism and non-silence, envelope/filter behaviour, and real-time note-on/note-off/stealing for a noise voice. UK English throughout.

## Minimal implementation

- Extend the schema with a discriminated noise oscillator variant (`type: "noise"`), keeping `detune` semantics and rejecting unknown oscillator fields.
- In the engine, widen the voice node union to a small startable/stoppable contract; for noise, create an `AudioBufferSourceNode` whose buffer comes from `src/audio/noise.ts` seeded by `oscillator.seed` (fixed default), with the same envelope curve and filter wiring as oscillators.
- Keep the oscillator branch structurally unchanged so byte-identical output is preserved; add the tests.

## Constraints

- No `Math.random`, no wall clock — the generator is the only entropy source.
- No new runtime dependencies; the noise buffer is produced by the shared seeded generator.
- Browser-safe: no Node-only imports in instrument modules.

**Key Files:**

- `src/instruments/schema.ts` — **Extend.** Noise oscillator variant + seed validation.
- `src/instruments/engine.ts` — **Extend.** Noise voice construction/teardown on both render paths.
- `src/instruments/schema.test.ts` — **Extend.** Accept/reject matrix for the noise variant.
- `src/instruments/engine.test.ts` — **Extend.** Determinism, non-silence, envelope, filter and real-time noise tests.
- `src/audio/noise.ts` — **Reuse.** Seeded noise-buffer generator.

# Per-note voice dispatch

**Parent:** TF-0MVEWKZ1R0011VFZ | **Type:** feature

> **Goal:** As a game developer, I want one instrument whose note-on dispatches to a per-note voice definition, so a single preset can voice a whole drum kit (note 36 kick, 38 snare, …) instead of one timbre stretched across the register.

## Context

Operator decision (Appendix Q5): extend the instrument definition with an optional per-note `voices` map — one YAML preset, one engine path, CLI unchanged. Today `renderInstrument` and `createRealtimeInstrument` render every note with the single top-level oscillator/envelope/filter, and `resolveInstrumentDefinition` returns exactly one definition for the CLI `--preset` path.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The definition schema accepts an optional `voices` map keyed by MIDI note number (0–127, integer keys); each entry validates as an override of `oscillator` (including the noise variant), `envelope` and optional `filter`; a malformed key or value is rejected with an actionable UK-English error naming the offending note/field.
2. A definition without `voices` renders exactly as before — the committed golden hashes are unchanged and `determinism.test.ts` stays green without regeneration.
3. With `voices`, the engine resolves each note-on to its mapped voice definition on **both** the offline and real-time paths (allocation, same-note retrigger and oldest-voice stealing still go through `VoiceManager`).
4. Notes with no entry in `voices` are ignored deterministically: no voice is allocated, they contribute silence, and a render of only unmapped notes is silent while mapped notes in the same sequence still sound.
5. Tests cover: override validation (accept/reject), per-note selection (different notes produce measurably different renders), unmapped-note silence in a mixed sequence, polyphony across kit voices (simultaneous notes independent), and unchanged behaviour for definitions without `voices`.

## Minimal implementation

- Add the optional `voices` map to the definition type and validator (reuse the existing oscillator/envelope/filter validators per entry).
- Add a small internal resolver `definitionForNote(definition, note)` used by both engine paths; skip unmapped notes at event-consumption time.
- Add the tests.

## Constraints

- Keep the existing single-voice code path byte-identical (golden hashes prove it).
- No new runtime dependencies; browser-safe.

**Key Files:**

- `src/instruments/schema.ts` — **Extend.** Optional `voices` map + per-entry validation.
- `src/instruments/engine.ts` — **Extend.** Per-note definition resolution and unmapped-note skip.
- `src/instruments/schema.test.ts` — **Extend.** `voices` accept/reject matrix.
- `src/instruments/engine.test.ts` — **Extend.** Dispatch, silence and polyphony tests.
- `src/instruments/voice-manager.ts` — **Reuse.** Allocation/retrigger/stealing policy.
data.title: Per-note voice dispatch

# Six-voice drum kit

**Parent:** TF-0MVEWKZ1R0011VFZ | **Type:** feature

> **Goal:** As a game developer, I want a `drum-kit` preset whose six voices map to GM notes — kick 36, snare 38, closed hat 42, open hat 46, crash 49, clap 39 — so GM percussion patterns sound like a real kit instead of one tuned sine.

## Context

Operator decisions: core six voices (Appendix Q3), one instrument with per-note dispatch via the `voices` map (Q5), noise oscillator with `color` + optional `seed` (Q4). The legacy `percussion` preset (`presets/instruments/percussion.yaml`) stays registered as the single-voice fallback. This child builds the kit content (voice models + preset); the golden-case and CLI verification live in the following child.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `presets/instruments/drum-kit.yaml` defines preset id `drum-kit`, name `Drum Kit`, category `Drums`, with six `voices` entries for notes 36, 38, 42, 46, 49 and 39, and validates through `validateInstrumentDefinition` (loadable by `loadBundledInstrumentPresets`).
2. Voice synthesis follows the documented models: **kick (36)** pitched with a fast pitch drop plus a short click transient; **snare (38)** a pitched body plus noise; **closed hat (42)** and **open hat (46)** filtered noise with short vs longer decay; **crash (49)** bright filtered noise with the longest decay; **clap (39)** a noise burst envelope with several distinct short bursts. Each noise-based voice uses the noise oscillator with its own seed.
3. All six voices render **non-silent** and are **measurably distinct** from each other using the shared analysis helpers (band energy + spectral centroid + decay time): kick has the lowest centroid and a short decay; closed hat decays faster than open hat; crash has the longest decay; clap is distinct from snare by burst structure and band profile.
4. Kit voice parameters are documented in code (per-voice docblocks stating the synthesis recipe and why), and the YAML carries comments explaining the GM note map.
5. Per-note dispatch works end to end for the kit: a render of the six GM notes sounds six different voices, and a same-note retrigger behaves like the existing engine (documented expectation, tested).
6. All errors, comments and docblocks are UK English.

## Minimal implementation

- Add `src/instruments/drum-kit.ts` holding the six voice definitions as typed `InstrumentDefinition`-compatible overrides, exported for tests and reuse.
- Add `presets/instruments/drum-kit.yaml` mirroring those definitions so the preset loader registers the kit.
- Add `src/instruments/drum-kit.test.ts` asserting audibility, distinctness and dispatch for the six notes.

## Constraints

- Six voices only — extending beyond the core six is a recorded follow-up, not this item.
- Every voice must render deterministically from its seeded noise/oscillator parameters (no clocks, no `Math.random`).
- Backward compatibility: do not modify `presets/instruments/percussion.yaml`.

**Key Files:**

- `src/instruments/drum-kit.ts` — **New.** Six kit voice models with documented synthesis.
- `presets/instruments/drum-kit.yaml` — **New.** `drum-kit` preset with the six-voice map.
- `src/instruments/drum-kit.test.ts` — **New.** Audibility, distinctness and dispatch tests.
- `src/instruments/__tests__/helpers.ts` — **Reuse.** Band-energy, decay and centroid assertions.
- `presets/instruments/percussion.yaml` — **Unchanged.** Legacy single-voice fallback.
data.title: Six-voice drum kit

# Re-voice leitmotif action percussion

**Parent:** TF-0MVEWKZ1R0011VFZ | **Type:** feature

> **Goal:** As a game developer, I want the shipped action cue's percussion voiced through the drum kit, so the leitmotif MIDI demonstrates the platform's real drum capability instead of a single sine.

## Context

`scripts/sequences/author-leitmotif.ts` is the single source of truth for `assets/music/leitmotif-action.mid`; its percussion track uses GM channel 9 notes 36/38/42/49 and is named `percussion (ToneForge: percussion, GM ch9)`. `author-leitmotif.test.ts` asserts byte-identity of the committed files against a fresh run. Operator decision (Q6): re-voice the action cue only, notes unchanged; the menu file has no percussion and stays drum-free.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `author-leitmotif.ts` names the percussion track for the kit (`percussion (ToneForge: drum-kit, GM ch9)`) and documents the note-to-voice mapping in a comment.
2. The percussion **notes, velocities and timings are unchanged** — this is a re-voicing, not a re-composition; a test asserts the percussion event set (notes/velocities/ticks) still equals the pre-change arrangement.
3. `npm run regenerate:leitmotif-music` regenerates `assets/music/leitmotif-action.mid`, which is committed; `npm run regenerate:leitmotif-music` is idempotent (a second run produces identical bytes).
4. `scripts/sequences/author-leitmotif.test.ts` is updated for the new track name and remains byte-identity green; `assets/music/leitmotif-menu.mid` bytes are **unchanged**.
5. The kit renders the regenerated file's percussion non-silently through `--preset drum-kit` (verified here or in the CLI-integration child, whichever lands the assertion).

## Minimal implementation

- Update the percussion track name and the mapping comment in the authoring script.
- Add the arrangement-preservation assertion (notes/velocities/ticks unchanged) to the test.
- Regenerate both files with the sanctioned npm script and commit the action file only.

## Constraints

- Do not add or move drum hits; new parts are out of scope.
- Regeneration must go through `npm run regenerate:leitmotif-music` only.

**Key Files:**

- `scripts/sequences/author-leitmotif.ts` — **Extend.** Kit track name + mapping comment.
- `scripts/sequences/author-leitmotif.test.ts` — **Extend.** New track name + arrangement-preservation assertions.
- `assets/music/leitmotif-action.mid` — **Regenerated.** Committed deliverable.
- `assets/music/leitmotif-menu.mid` — **Unchanged.** No percussion track.
data.title: Re-voice leitmotif action percussion

# Documentation for noise oscillators and drum kit

**Parent:** TF-0MVEWKZ1R0011VFZ | **Type:** docs

> **Goal:** As a music-technician, I want the guides and module docs to describe the noise oscillator and the six-voice drum kit (and mark `percussion` as legacy), so the shipped music and the documented capability agree.

## Context

`docs/guides/midi-sequences-howto.md` §4 has a percussion track row using `percussion`, §"Channels, programs and controllers" describes percussion routing, and the "The percussion preset" section states there is no noise generator. `docs/modules/instruments.md` documents six oscillator-only presets, the schema and the determinism mechanism. Both must reflect the noise oscillator, the `drum-kit` preset and the regenerated action file.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `docs/guides/midi-sequences-howto.md`: the §4 percussion row names `drum-kit`; the channels/programs notes describe routing channel 9 through the kit; "The percussion preset" section is replaced by a **"The drum kit"** section documenting the six voices, their synthesis approach (pitched kick, noise-based snare/hats/crash/clap), the GM note map (36/38/42/46/49/39), CLI selection (`toneforge instrument play <file.mid> --preset drum-kit`), and how the action cue uses it.
2. `docs/modules/instruments.md`: the schema documentation covers the noise oscillator (`{ type: "noise", color, seed? }`, three colours, seeded determinism), the preset table gains a `drum-kit` row (six voices) and marks `percussion` as the legacy single-voice fallback, and the determinism section states the seed default/override rule and the sanctioned regeneration command.
3. No stale claims remain: `grep` for "there is no noise generator" and equivalent statements returns nothing across `docs/` and `README.md`.
4. Boilerplate updated wherever the preset family is listed (README and any docs index that enumerates the presets), plus the module file header comments in `src/instruments/index.ts` and `src/instruments/schema.ts` reflecting noise voices and per-note dispatch.
5. All prose is UK English and British spelling; markdown links resolve to real files; the docs render without broken tables.

## Minimal implementation

- Rewrite the two percussion sections in the howto and add the drum-kit examples.
- Extend `docs/modules/instruments.md` (schema, preset table, determinism, limitations/follow-ups).
- Sweep `README.md` and module headers for preset lists and stale noise claims.

## Constraints

- Documentation-only change: no production code, no test expectations altered.
- Do not document voices or options that do not exist in the shipped schema — verify against `presets/instruments/drum-kit.yaml`.

**Key Files:**

- `docs/guides/midi-sequences-howto.md` — **Rewrite.** Percussion track table, routing notes and the kit section.
- `docs/modules/instruments.md` — **Extend.** Noise oscillator, kit preset row, determinism and limitations.
- `./README.md` — **Update.** Preset family mention.
- `src/instruments/index.ts` — **Update.** Module header docblock.
- `src/instruments/schema.ts` — **Update.** Schema docblocks for noise/voices.
data.title: Documentation for noise oscillators and drum kit

Final disposition: no code change was required under this item.

- The fix for this specific failure landed on `dev` in commit 2dbbf36 under sibling item TF-0MVE3XFZ5005TPHP (the same commit rewrote both serve tests in `src/cli.runtime.start.integration.test.ts`, including the quit-command test: 60 s readiness/fallback budget instead of 8-10 s, explicit 120 s per-test timeout instead of the global 20 s, stderr capture for actionable failures, 5 s SIGKILL escalation).
- Verification (read-only, cached): three recent full-suite runs — f67db925 and 4a499c81 (HEAD 10901dd) and 7bb92306 (current dev tip state, 233 files / 4900 tests, exit 0) — all report `✓ src/cli.runtime.start.integration.test.ts (19 tests)`, which includes `shuts down cleanly on a quit command`. No failing entry exists for this test at HEAD.
- AC2 (documentation) is satisfied by the extensive harness-timing comments added to the test file in 2dbbf36. I considered adding a cross-reference to `SERVE_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS` in the `vitest.config.ts` timeout comment, but a comment-only commit would force two additional contended full-suite runs (changed-scope falls back to full scope for this repo), so I dropped it: the host was running 8+ concurrent suites from other projects and this item's finish attempt already exhausted the 600 s test-slot wait. The existing test-file documentation is sufficient.

Marking completed / in_review on the strength of the already-landed fix and the cached green suite at HEAD.
